title: 1962 AHSME Problem 7
statement: Let the bisectors of the exterior angles at \(B\) and \(C\) of triangle \(ABC\) meet at \(D.\) Then, if all measurements are in degrees, angle \(BDC\) equals:

solutions.text:
The angles of triangle \(BDC\) at \(B\) and \(C\) are \(90^\circ-\frac{B}{2}\) and \(90^\circ-\frac{C}{2}.\) Thus \[ \begin{aligned} \angle BDC &=180^\circ-\left(90^\circ-\frac B2\right) \\ &\quad-\left(90^\circ-\frac C2\right)\\ &=\frac{B+C}{2} \\ &=\frac{180^\circ-A}{2}. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Each exterior-angle bisector makes an angle \(90^\circ-\frac{B}{2}\) or \(90^\circ-\frac{C}{2}\) with a side
Apply the angle sum in triangle \(BDC\) and use \(B+C=180^\circ-A\)
